name: cycle
description: A depends on B depends on A, via parent_task_id. Should not happen, and it will. HierarchyFixture permits this on purpose -- it does not enforce acyclicity -- so this graph loads; what the propagation code does with it is the decision this fixture records.

nodes.label: Leaf under the cycle -- without this, leaf_ids() is empty and no leaf-starting walk ever enters the loop

notes: Decision: detect the cycle and refuse (raise), rather than silently breaking at a depth limit. Matches Chain's own traversal code, which treats a cycle as a defensive guard against corrupt data, not a case to paper over. A naive walk-the-parent-chain implementation loops forever here -- that's the whole point of this fixture. task_in_cycle exists only so leaf_ids() is non-empty and a leaf-starting walk actually reaches the cycle.
